                    ### Question
                    A 42-year-old man comes to the physician for 1 month of worsening right knee pain. He has not had any trauma other than stubbing his toe 3 days ago at the garage where he works as a mechanic. Examination of the right knee shows swelling and erythema with fluctuance over the inferior patella. There is tenderness on palpation of the patella but no joint line tenderness or warmth. The range of flexion is limited because of the pain. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's symptoms?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Inflammation of the patellar tendon
opb. Noninflammatory degeneration of the joint
opc. Infection of the joint
opd. Deposition of crystals in the joint
ope. Inflammation of periarticular fluid-filled sac

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
The patient's symptoms of right knee pain, swelling, erythema with fluctuance, and tenderness on palpation suggest a possible joint effusion, which is often associated with inflammation or infection. The presence of fluctuance indicates a collection of fluid, likely in a bursa or joint space. The absence of joint line tenderness makes meniscal injury less likely, and the limited range of motion due to pain does not strongly support noninflammatory degeneration. Given the clinical presentation, the most likely underlying cause is inflammation of a periarticular fluid-filled sac, such as bursitis. This aligns with the chain indicating that swelling and fluctuance over the inferior patella suggest possible bursitis, confirming the option of inflammation of periarticular fluid-filled sac as the most likely cause.
